There was a time when all of America believed that the future of the physical world could be radically different. The engineers of the mid-1900s put a man on the moon in eight years, designed and built planes and submarines from scratch in under three, and conceived of building things we wouldn’t even be able to dream up today.

Today, the last of the engineers who imagined and built these systems are retiring. As they go, we lose not only the engineering knowledge gained from their decades of imagination and trial-and-error, but also the spirit that made that imagination possible.

Amca is working day-in and day-out to restore America’s ability to engineer anything that our critical systems depend on, and reinvigorate the cycle of creation that allows imagination to shape physical reality. We rapidly develop and manufacture new critical components and subsystems required to build and sustain the planes, military vehicles, and core infrastructure America needs. By restoring the capability of our antiquated supply chains, we increase the country’s capacity to imagine and realize new systems, and make a physical world that looks very different from today.

Software Engineer

Overview

Amca is hiring software engineering interns to build the systems that turn decades of engineering knowledge into structured, usable data. The work broadly falls into two areas: software that digitizes, labels, and organizes millions of technical drawings, designs, and engineering documents, and a custom software suite that makes engineers and factory teams faster across the factories and Protoshop.

Interns work on real production problems with real users on the other end. The tools built here shape how quickly hardware gets designed, built, and shipped.

Responsibilities

- Build pipelines that ingest, digitize, label, and structure large volumes of technical drawings, CAD files, and engineering documentation

- Develop internal tools that speed up engineering and manufacturing workflows across the factories and Protoshop, using data we've codified from our acquired factories or by observing the current practices of our factories.

- Design and ship full stack products and features

- Work directly with engineers and production teams to understand their bottlenecks, turn them into software, measure the software’s impact, and improve product

- Improve the performance, reliability, and scalability of existing systems

- Write clean, tested, well-documented pseudo-code and code and take part in code review

Basic Qualifications

- Currently pursuing a bachelor's or master's degree in computer science, computer or software engineering, mathematics, physics, or a related field

- Understand and experience using storage systems, cloud infrastructure, and front-end frameworks

- Learns quickly, picks up unfamiliar tools without hand-holding, can understand and write detailed documentation, and takes ownership of everything you build

- Communicates clearly with both technical and non-technical teammates on plans, updates, and blockers

Preferred Skills and Experience

- Strong fluency in using AI coding tools to build and ship efficiently, but does not rely on these tools to write code, nor trust these tools entirely to write flawless code. You are responsible for understanding every line an agent writes.

- Strong git habits, especially on shared repos, including clear commits, branching, pull requests, reviews

- Experience shipping full-stack features or applications to production, through an internship, project team, or personal project

- Proficiency in one or more of TypeScript, React, Go, Python, or SQL

At Delta Faucet, we are committed to transforming everyday experiences with water through innovative products and exceptional service. As a leader in the plumbing industry, we take pride in our dedication to quality, sustainability, and customer satisfaction. We believe that diverse perspectives strengthen our mission to create solutions that inspire and elevate the lives of all our customers. We welcome individuals from all backgrounds to join us on this journey toward inclusivity and excellence.

Your Role at Delta Faucet

Delta Faucet Company has an opportunity for a Hardware Engineering Co-op to join our Connected Water Team to help deliver the next generation of product features and technology to our customers. In this role, you will support the development of new digital products through hands-on work with embedded systems and real product hardware.

You will spend most of your days in the lab doing hands-on and varied tasks: soldering and reworking assemblies, programming and bringing up circuit boards, running electrical and functional tests, laying out PCBs, and keeping our engineering lab and its equipment running as smoothly as possible.

You will report to the engineering manager and sit with the project teams, not apart from them. Within your first few weeks you will be assigned specific tasks, projects, and test processes to own — meaning you make the calls there, you document how it works, and you are the person others ask about it. When you find a better way to do something, we want to hear it, and we will give you a straight answer either way.

Every part of the role is scoped so that the skills you leave with — test methodology, debugging discipline, documentation, lab ownership — are the ones that help you with the rest of your college work and prepare you for your future career.

Responsibilities:

Build and Rework

- Solder, rework, and modify through-hole and surface-mount assemblies for prototypes, test fixtures, and engineering samples.
- Assemble and wire test fixtures, harnesses, and benchtop setups from schematics and written instructions.
- Program, flash, and bring up circuit boards; verify power rails, signal integrity, and basic functionality on new builds.

Test and Debug

- Execute electrical, functional, and reliability tests on products and subassemblies, and record results accurately.
- Investigate test failures: reproduce the issue, isolate it to a component or subsystem, and document what you found so an engineer can act on it.
- Write and maintain basic test scripts and data-logging routines to automate repetitive measurements.
- Operate and troubleshoot standard bench equipment — oscilloscopes, DMMs, power supplies, function generators, data acquisition systems, environmental chambers.

Design Support

- Produce PCB layouts for test fixtures, adapter boards, and design revisions under engineering guidance.
- Review schematics and layouts for manufacturability and testability, and raise concerns before boards are ordered.
- Suggest product and process improvements based on what you observe on the bench

Lab and Calibration Ownership

- Organize and manage the engineering lab: equipment inventory, tool and fixture storage, consumable stock, workspace layout, and bench readiness.
- Run the equipment calibration program — track calibration due dates, coordinate with vendors, maintain certificates, and keep instruments in a known-good state.
- Establish and document standard operating procedures for test setups, lab safety, and equipment use so results are repeatable across people and across time.
- Maintain clear technical documentation: test reports, procedures, wiring diagrams, bring-up notes, and change records.

Where this goes

We treat this co-op as the first step in a career here, not a temporary set of hands. The scope is designed to grow with you:

- In your first term, you will learn our products, our lab, and our test methods, supporting engineers on defined tasks.
- As you demonstrate judgment, you will take ownership of specific test areas, fixtures, and the calibration program — work that is yours, with your name on it.
- Strong co-ops are invited back for additional terms with expanded responsibility, and we actively look to convert high performers into full-time engineering or test roles at graduation.

You will finish with a portfolio of real work: products you helped validate, fixtures you designed, procedures you wrote, and failures you tracked down. That is experience that transfers anywhere — and we would rather you build it here and stay.

Qualifications

- Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or master’s degree in electrical engineering, Electrical Engineering Technology, or related field
- Demonstrated hands-on experience — coursework labs, senior design, competition teams (IEEE, Robotics, etc.), maker projects, or personal builds. Show us what you have made.
- Excellent soldering experience, including small components and SMT rework
- Foundational understanding of analog and digital circuits. Comfort reading schematics and interpreting datasheets and basic specifications.
- Careful, methodical work habits. In test engineering, sloppy data is worse than no data, and this role is built on trustworthy measurements.
- Clear written communication — you will write procedures and failure reports that other people rely on.
- Familiarity with microcontrollers, embedded systems, and electronics lab equipment
- Strong problem-solving skills, curiosity, and a willingness to learn in a hands-on engineering environment
- Interest in IoT, connected products, or consumer electronics is a plus

The target compensation for the role is $22.00 hour.

At Delta Faucet Company, our people are our greatest assets. We value different perspectives and fostering an inclusive environment. You’ll have the opportunity to shape the future of our brand, working alongside passionate professionals committed to excellence and innovation. Join us to lead progressive growth and make a significant impact within a leading organization.

Here are some of the benefits we offer for your personal and professional growth:

The Production Allocation Engineering Intern will support the daily and monthly processes used to track, validate, allocate, and report oil, gas, and water production across the asset. Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors to first responders, soldiers in battlefield scenarios, and beyond.

About the Role:

The core of our system is the computer vision algorithms that allow drones to understand the world around them. You will architect and implement the algorithms that run on every drone powered by Skydio as part of a world class computer vision and deep learning team with researchers who have pushed the state of the art in academia and industry.

As a Research Intern, you will be paired up with one or more members of our core software development team, assuming direct ownership of a project that meaningfully advances the capabilities of our team and products.

If you have a strong foundation in math, theory, and software development and you are interested in directly contributing to the development of the next generation of autonomy algorithms and pushing them into real products, we would love to hear from you.

Areas of Responsibility:

- Core Simulator Architecture: Design, implement, and evolve the foundational architecture of the Skydio Simulator, ensuring it scales across vehicle types, environments, and use cases.

- Physics and Dynamics: Improve and extend physics models governing vehicle motion, interactions with the environment, and dynamic agents.

- Sensor and Hardware Simulation: Build high-fidelity simulations of cameras, IMUs, and other onboard components, including timing, noise characteristics, and hardware behavior.

- Autonomy Stack Integration: Run and validate the full Skydio autonomy stack in simulation, ensuring consistency between simulated and real-world behavior.

- Feature Development on Top of the Core: Implement simulator capabilities that unlock new workflows for customers and internal autonomy engineers, from training scenarios to advanced testing modes.

- Performance and Fidelity: Profile, optimize, and improve simulator performance while continuously pushing realism and accuracy.

What You’ll Do:

- Develop core simulator components in C++ and Python, working close to real-time constraints.

- Collaborate with autonomy, perception, and controls engineers to align simulation behavior with real-world systems.

- Debug complex interactions between physics, sensors, autonomy logic, and rendering.

- Help shape the long-term technical direction of the simulator as both a product and an internal platform.

- Contribute to documentation and shared understanding of how the simulator works internally.

Qualifications:

- Strong software engineering experience with C++ and Python.

- Experience building complex systems where performance, determinism, or correctness matter.

- Comfort reasoning about time-synchronized systems, state machines, or real-time execution.

- Ability to work in a large, evolving codebase with multiple stakeholders.

- Interest in robotics, simulation, or physical systems (prior robotics experience is a plus, not a requirement).

Bonus Experience:

- Robotics, simulation, game engines, or real-time systems.

- Physics engines, sensor modeling, or hardware abstraction layers.

- Multithreaded or low-latency system design.

- Experience debugging systems that span software and physical behavior.

Applicants must be authorized to work in the U.S. independently. At this time, we do not offer visa sponsorship for this role.

The Summer 2027 Data Science Research & Development (DSRD) Graduate Internship offers an exciting opportunity for graduate students to apply advanced data science, machine learning, artificial intelligence, and software engineering techniques to solve complex clinical and healthcare challenges.

This internship is designed for highly motivated individuals who are passionate about leveraging cutting-edge technology to improve healthcare outcomes, advance medical research, and drive innovation across the healthcare industry.

As a member of the Data Science Research & Development team, the intern will collaborate with a multidisciplinary group of researchers, data scientists, machine learning engineers, and software developers to develop innovative solutions utilizing clinical, medical, and healthcare insurance data. Interns will gain hands-on experience working on high-impact research initiatives that directly support healthcare transformation through advanced analytics, predictive modeling, artificial intelligence, graph technologies, computer vision, and generative AI.

The internship is structured around four specialized research tracks, allowing participants to align their work with their technical background and research interests:

- Knowledge Graphs: Design and optimize graph-based healthcare data models, develop GraphQL interfaces, and leverage Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and GraphRAG architectures to enhance predictive analytics and knowledge discovery.
- Medical Imaging: Build image processing pipelines and develop computer vision models for clinical image analysis, anatomical segmentation, and pathology classification.
- Predictive Modeling: Develop machine learning models focused on healthcare risk prediction, disease progression, and patient outcome forecasting while ensuring model explainability and fairness.
- AI Applications: Design and evaluate advanced AI agent frameworks, natural language processing solutions, prompt engineering strategies, and clinical information extraction workflows using emerging generative AI technologies.

Participants will contribute to innovative research projects, assist with the design and development of analytical solutions, conduct model evaluation and experimentation, and communicate findings to technical and business audiences. Through mentorship, collaboration, and applied research, interns will strengthen their technical expertise while gaining valuable exposure to healthcare data science, artificial intelligence, and enterprise-scale innovation.

SUMMARY OF JOB RESPONSIBILITIES

This job has the goal of providing the opportunity to acquire practical experience through direct exposure to the related business line(s) and to develop the next generation of diverse business professionals. To that end, the program will provide hands-on training and experience in the business line, expose the various career opportunities in the business line and related areas, and prepare participants for positions in the business.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Bachelor’s degree.
- Pursuance of a graduate degree full or part-time in an accredited college or university.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Currently pursuing a Master's or Ph.D. degree in Computer Science, Biomedical Informatics, Data Science, Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related quantitative discipline.
- Strong programming experience in Python.
- Experience utilizing modern data science libraries such as NumPy, Pandas, Scikit-learn, PyTorch, and/or TensorFlow.
- Proficiency in SQL and relational database concepts.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS
1. Communicate effectively. This position displays effective communication skills while interacting directly with colleagues, clientele, and/or other internal or external constituencies in the planning of assignments and the resolution of day-to-day operational problems.

2. Under supervision, provide professional services as appropriate to the day-to-day operating objectives of the area. Receives guidance, training, and mentoring from senior personnel in planning and carrying out activities and assignments.

3. Undertake and/or participate in projects and programs designed to develop professional skills and expertise appropriate to the needs of the organization.

4. Participate in the planning and implementation of unit projects and initiatives within area of expertise and ability.

5. As specifically requested by management, conducts research and reporting inclusive of recommendations or alternative proposals for action.

6. Undertake related studies or enrichment programs as appropriate to the specific objectives of the operating unit.

7. Perform miscellaneous job-related duties as assigned.
